jobs.description: Assistant Professor, Art & Design, Tenure Track 499125 Grand Forks, North Dakota, United States Full-time Faculty View favorites Salary/Position Classification $60,000+ Dependent on Experience, 9-month contract, Exempt 40 hours per week This position will work onsite at the UND Grand Forks, ND campus Purpose of Position The Department of Art & Design is seeking to hire a tenure-track Assistant Professor in any studio art with a specialization in Emerging Technologies and Artificial Intelligence (New Media) in the Visual Arts. In addition to salary and benefits, the Burgum Arts & Sciences Endowed Chair will receive professional development funding annually to support travel as well as equipment for teaching and creative activities/research. The successful candidate will be expected to teach undergraduate and graduate courses, produce creative activities/scholarship, and do service that contributes to the mission of the department, the college, and the university. The Department of Art & Design is housed in the College of Arts & Sciences and currently offers an MFA in Visual Arts, BFAs in Visual Arts and Graphic Design, a BA in Visual Arts, and minors in Art History, Graphic Design, and Visual Arts. The department is the recipient of a generous annually recurring endowment from the Myers Foundations that supports a robust visiting artists program, curation of art exhibitions, and resources to enhance student teaching and learning among other activities. Established in 1883, the University of North Dakota is the oldest research university in North Dakota. Founded with a strong liberal arts foundation, it is the state’s flagship university and is classified by the Carnegie Foundation as having very high research activity. UND offers degrees in more than 225 fields of study and enrolls nearly 16,000 students. It is the home of the state’s only School of Law and School of Medicine. The School of Medicine and Health Sciences has major initiatives in rural and public health, and Aerospace is home to one of the first and largest unmanned aerial vehicle programs in the world. UND is located in Grand Forks, North Dakota, a vibrant college town of over 57,000 people located on the border of North Dakota and Minnesota. Short commutes, a great public-school system, high-quality medical facilities, low crime, ample parks and theaters, and a cost of living below that found in large American cities are some of Grand Forks’ advantages. Ranked as one of the top 5 Best Small College Towns, and America’s Best Hockey Town, Grand Forks offers stellar quality of life without the metropolitan hassles. UND and the College of Arts & Sciences value perspectives from a broad range of backgrounds and seek applicants to help students succeed. The University of North Dakota is supportive of dual-career assistance both within the University and the local community. Please contact UND’s Recruiting Manager, Hannah Whalen (Hannah.Whalen@UND.edu), to explore dual-career opportunities. Duties & Responsibilities The successful applicant will receive a contract with an approximate distribution of 52% teaching (3/2), 38% research/creative activity, and 10% service. More specific duties and responsibilities for this position include: Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in a studio art with an emphasis on the integration of emerging technologies and AI (new media) Advise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students Serve as a catalyst for attracting and supporting graduate students in the MFA in Visual Arts Program Establish a solid and productive research program with emphasis in area of specialization, including seeking extramural funding to support individual and collaborative projects aligned with the UND LEADS Strategic Plan Submit an annual report of creative/research, teaching, and public outreach activities supported by professional development funds provided by the Burgum Arts & Sciences Endowed Chair Endowment. jobs.title: Assistant Professor/Extension Sugarbeet Agronomist
jobs.description: Previous JobJob TitleAssistant Professor/Extension Sugarbeet Agronomist Next JobApply for JobJob ID2959848 Business UnitNorth Dakota State University LocationFargo Posted09/02/2026 Full/Part TimeFull-Time DepartmentExt Plant Science Close DateOpen Until Filled Add to My Favorite JobsEmail this Job Position Information Description & Details:This is a 12-month, tenure-track position (70% Extension, 20% research, and 10% service) in the Department of Plant Sciences at North Dakota State University. The position is jointly funded by North Dakota State University (NDSU) and the University of Minnesota (U of M). The incumbent will be based at NDSU and expected to work in both North Dakota and Minnesota. The successful candidate will lead the development and implementation of Extension and applied research programs focused on weed management and cropping systems for sugarbeet production. Responsibilities include developing educational materials and programs for producers, industry professionals, and Extension personnel; conducting applied research; publishing results in peer-reviewed journals and Extension publications; delivering science-based recommendations to support successful sugarbeet production; and pursuing extramural funding. The incumbent will build collaborative partnerships (including equipment and resources) with NDSU faculty and staff, specifically in the NDSU Departments of Plant Sciences and Plant Pathology, Microbiology, and Biotechnology; with the University of Minnesota; the Sugarbeet Research and Education Board; USDA sugarbeet researchers; allied industry partners in the sugarbeet industry; and sugarbeet cooperatives. Extension programming will use a variety of delivery methods, including print and digital publications, web resources, presentations, field days, workshops, radio, television, and virtual platforms. Additional responsibilities include coordinating Extension and research activities across department and college faculty and Extension agents across a range of agronomic disciplines, and advising graduate students.Hiring Range: $85,000 +Pay is based on several factors, including budget, labor market, prior experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and/or certification and other business considerations. Minimum Qualifications:An earned PhD in weed science, crop science, agronomy, or a related field by the hire date.Demonstrated experience in applied crop production and/or in weed management.Demonstrated ability to work effectively with university faculty, Extension personnel, producer organizations, and the public.Demonstrated ability to conduct applied research, interpret and communicate findings, and develop science-based recommendations for producers.Proven ability to collaborate effectively with stakeholders, colleagues, and multidisciplinary research teams. Proficiency with computer applications and relevant technologies.Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.Possession of a valid US driver's license or the ability to obtain one by the date of hire.Possession of, or ability to obtain by the hire date, a valid pesticide applicator’s license in North Dakota and Minnesota. Preferred Qualifications:Farm background or practical agricultural production experience.Experience with sugarbeet production systems.Experience in Extension, teaching, stakeholder engagement, or agricultural outreach.Research, industry, or applied agricultural experience in crop production and weed management.Demonstrated success in developing competitive grant proposals, securing extramural funding, and publishing research findings.Knowledge of agricultural regulations and experience navigating regulatory frameworks.Experience with precision agriculture, crop data management, or related digital agriculture technologies.Application Deadline:October 1, 2026, or until filled. jobs.description: Previous JobJob TitleJunior Research Economist/ Research Assistant Professor Next JobApply for JobJob ID2959460 Business UnitNorth Dakota State University LocationFargo Posted07/27/2026 Full/Part TimeFull-Time DepartmentAES Agribusiness & Appld Econ Close DateOpen Until Filled Add to My Favorite JobsEmail this Job Position Information Description & Details:Junior Research Economist at the Rank of Research Assistant ProfessorThe Department of Agribusiness and Applied Economics at North Dakota State University seeks to appoint a promising early-career research economist to conduct grant-funded research, policy analysis, and market intelligence on U.S. agricultural policy and trade issues. The position will support applied research and stakeholder-oriented analysis on commodity markets, trade policy, and global market developments affecting U.S. and North Dakota producers and agribusinesses. The appointment is a full-time, non-tenure track position at the rank of Research Assistant Professor. The initial appointment will be for two years with the possibility of extension based on performance and continued availability of external funding.The successful candidate will join a research and outreach program led by Dr. Sandro Steinbach at North Dakota State University and affiliated with the Center for Agricultural Policy and Trade Studies. The position will help develop timely and rigorous analysis of agricultural trade, commodity market conditions, input market developments, policy changes, and global disruptions that shape opportunities and risks for U.S. and North Dakota agriculture. jobs.description: Previous JobJob TitleVisiting Lecturers Next JobApply for JobJob ID2959151 Business UnitNorth Dakota State University LocationFargo Posted08/05/2026 Full/Part TimeFull-Time DepartmentSchool of Education Close DateOpen Until Filled Add to My Favorite JobsEmail this Job Position Information Visiting LecturerPhysical Education and/or Health EducationSchool of EducationNorth Dakota State University The School of Education at North Dakota State University (NDSU) invites inquiries, nominations, and applications for a 1-year non-tenure-track, nine (9) month Lecturer position with a primary focus on Physical Education and/or Health Education (PE/HE) to begin January 2027. This position will consist of 80% teacher (4 courses per semester), 10% supervision of student teachers (5 student teachers/year), and 10% service with the opportunity to teach in the summer. The position includes a possible renewable contract. NDSU’s PE/HE programs include a stand-alone undergraduate physical education program (with both a K-12 licensing option and a coaching and physical activity leadership option), stand-alone health education major (5th-12th licensing), undergraduate Sport Coaching Certificate, as well as an online master’s program (Leadership in Physical Education and Sport Coaching [LPESC]). Both teacher preparation programs are accredited by CAEP and approximately 95% of teacher candidates double major in both content areas. The undergraduate programs emphasize experiential learning and best practices, incorporate a variety of technology tools and applications, and provide diverse and unique field experiences. The LPESC master’s program currently serves 35 practitioners from across the United States and other countries. Learn more about the undergraduate and graduate programs here: Physical Education: https://www.ndsu.edu/education/academic-areas/teacher-preparation/physical-education Health Education: https://www.ndsu.edu/education/academic-areas/teacher-preparation/health-education Sport Coaching Certificate: https://www.ndsu.edu/education/degree-programs/undergraduate-minor-certificate/certificate-in-sport-coaching LPESC: https://www.ndsu.edu/education/academic-areas/k-12-advanced-degrees/leadership-in-physical-education-sport-coaching The successful candidate will be able to teach courses in at least one or more of the undergraduate programs; supervise student teachers; provide service to the department, college, university, and community; work effectively with colleagues across disciplines and/or community organizations; and contribute to department governance while fostering a collaborative community across the School of Education. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONSMaster’s degree in Physical Education, Health Education, or closely related field from an accredited institutionPK-12 teaching experience in one of the program areasDemonstrated commitment to equity, access, and inclusionAbility to interact and collaborate effectively with a diversity of colleagues and studentsEffective oral and written communications skills PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONSPhD or EdD in Physical Education, Health Education or closely related field from an accredited institutionExperience teaching PETE/HETE coursesOnline teaching experience or online learning experiences as a studentActive participation in school-university collaborations (e.g., supervision of student teachers)Membership and involvement in professional organizations Salary: Commensurate with experience and qualifications. This position is benefited.
